biography: William is looking to move on from Microsoft after two years (by March), having gained buy-side experience and an understanding of hyperscaler operations. He is open to two or three types of roles, prioritizing career growth, optionality, and work-life balance. William is interested in continuing leasing and co-location acquisition, specifically on the sell-side for better compensation and a new market perspective. He is also interested in learning site development and site finding to unlock more job opportunities and add new skills. William is considering a business development role focused on strategic relationship management with hyperscalers, leveraging his understanding of their processes. He is open to international roles in countries with lower or no tax, such as Dubai. William will complete 24 months at Microsoft in March. He currently reports to Elvira, who manages Joanne, and is part of a team with Carlota, Hoiki, Christine, and Justina. William's current role involves managing 9 markets, although he should ideally have 3, with significant experience in Amsterdam, Poland, and Spain. Frustrations at Microsoft stem from increased bureaucracy, a 30% headcount reduction combined with a doubled workload due to unexpected AI deals, rigid processes struggling to adapt to market changes, and a difficult change in management style. These factors have led to 7 team members quitting this year, with no backfills, and many others looking to leave. William worked at CBRE for seven years, focusing on retail co-location acquisition, growing in seniority and accountability. He was an account manager for Kyndryl (formerly IBM and IBM Cloud) when he left, overseeing four or five supporting team members. His work at CBRE involved global geographical experience, including Latin America, Texas, Japan, and Europe, as well as deals in Pakistan. Kyndryl's strategy involved offloading archaic data centers through sale and leasebacks and moving to mainly leasing, which kept William busy. His role primarily involved delivery on existing accounts, though he was involved in pitching for new clients and winning initial deals, with dedicated business development directors handling new lead generation. William is currently involved in interview processes for three roles: a site selection manager, a leasing director, and a business director role. He is only genuinely interested in one of these opportunities because the other two are with hyperscalers, which he wants to move away from. The preferred company is not a hyperscaler. Ward presented a potential leasing role with Panattoni, a large industrial developer expanding into data centers across EMEA and India. Panattoni has hired a team from Colt Data Centre, led by Richard Wellbrock, and has identified 2.1 GW of development pipeline, with another 4.9 GW in earlier stages. They have 40 different capital partners and are open to selling/leasing powered land and building powered shells, potentially fitting out MEP later. Panattoni aims to lease to both hyperscalers and co-location operators. The preference is for someone with sell-side experience, but they are open to candidates from brokerage or buy-side hyperscalers. Ward will provide more details next week. William has limited experience with powered shell and powered land leasing, but is interested in the sell-side aspect. William acknowledges that transitioning from leasing to site selection/land development without prior land experience is challenging. He knows colleagues who made a similar transition but had M&A experience. He believes such a move might require an internal transfer at Microsoft to gain land experience or finding a role at a developer that allows him to learn land development alongside leasing. William has explored an internal land role at Microsoft. Ward suggests developers are increasingly looking for buy-side experience for commercial roles.

assessment.note: Ward Search's own judgement, not a researched fact.
